page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance built on KVM virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the configuration delivers 8 dedicated virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 16.0 GB RAM, adhering to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Architectural vector extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with hardware-assisted cryptographic AES instructions. Local storage is not included, requiring external cloud block storage for operational filesystems, and network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier throughput across multi-threaded computational workloads. While single-thread operations like stress-ng single-core tests (1313.59) and file compression tasks register in lower benchmark tiers, multi-threaded evaluations demonstrate balanced output. Geekbench scores reach 1168.0 for single-core and 4486.0 for multi-core processing, with software compilation tests via Clang scoring 6670.0. The PassMark CPU assessment recorded 8266.91, paired with memory read bandwidth of 50.07 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 37.35 GB/sec on writes.

The hardware configuration provides balanced resource utilization for compute workloads that do not demand extensive per-core RAM allocations. Because the instance lacks bundled local storage, storage performance is bound to attached network volumes. The combination of dedicated Intel Xeon cores, vector extensions, and 3 Gbps baseline network capacity makes this server profile functional for web serving, microservices architectures, build systems, and distributed caching nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual server configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of memory across 4 physical cores. Built on the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz under KVM virtualization, it features AVX-512 vector support and a 1:2 core-to-memory distribution. The instance does not include local disk storage, depending entirely on attached network volumes, and features a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic testing reflects average performance across multi-core execution, software compilation, and network-bound tasks, with a PassMark CPU score of 8266.91 and Geekbench multi-core score of 4486.0. Single-threaded benchmarks and compression rates place lower. The hardware profile offers balanced compute density for compilation workloads, container hosts, distributed caching tiers, and static web serving.
